body: @juanfont, I saw your comment https://github.com/juanfont/headscale/issues/1205#issuecomment-1542204670 but I think that adding the base fields from HostInfo will not affect the HeadScale in any way, because it is unlikely that TailScale will change the fields used in any way

Quoting the issue referred above:
> After discussing it with @kradalby, we reckon it would be safer/saner for Headscale if you just marshal the Machine.HostInfo as a string into gRPC, rather than transforming it into a proto object in Headscale. This way, if something changes (and it might from Tailscale side) Headscale would not be affected.

We cannot maintain all these field hand typed into the API, however just marshalling it as JSON and then unmarshalling it on the other side using `tailcfg.Hostinfo` would be fine. 

If this is implemented, it should also be part of the JSON output of `headscale nodes list --json` and it should have integration tests to verify the output. 

As mentioned in our contribution guidelines, all contributions needs tests and there are a few more tickboxes that has not been addressed.

body: @kradalby as someone who works on a web interface for Headscale I'm interested in seeing this PR merged. I'd be willing to also take it on and move it over the finish line if the original author is no longer available 😄

> I dont have a good solution, but I am more conservative to adding it than adding it for the sake of it. If you want to have a look and come up with a proposal I am willing to hear it.

I respectfully disagree with this perspective. Regardless of its limitations, a unified mechanism to check the client version is essential as it helps mitigate security vulnerabilities. While avoiding action may reduce the risk of introducing errors, it unfortunately does not address the underlying issues.


> We cannot maintain all these field hand typed into the API

May I ask why this is a concern? These fields are also utilized by Tailscale’s console, which is almost certainly stable. Following this approach would not introduce more compatibility issues than those present in Tailscale’s official instance.

> I respectfully disagree with this perspective. Regardless of its limitations, a unified mechanism to check the client version is essential as it helps mitigate security vulnerabilities. While avoiding action may reduce the risk of introducing errors, it unfortunately does not address the underlying issues.

I disagree with this perspective. If the version field specifically is needed, then I propose that being added.

> May I ask why this is a concern? These fields are also utilized by Tailscale’s console, which is almost certainly stable. Following this approach would not introduce more compatibility issues than those present in Tailscale’s official instance.

The alternative is this: https://github.com/juanfont/headscale/pull/942/files#diff-ac94c91f8ea84762d55b6932ef1466a2165984591d3e646360c5bb31b2130900R248

The fields do change, manually managing drift is not an option.

> The fields do change, manually managing drift is not an option.

I briefly checked HostInfo (not very thoroughly), and it seems there have been no breaking changes in recent years (I mean deleting or renaming a field). It does change, but only with the addition of new fields. Following general principles, writing a manual transformation function for this doesn’t seem to add much overhead. As for the fields that might be added in the future, we can simply ignore them. If they become useful to us, a random user who needs them will likely file an issue, and we can address it then. I don’t see anything wrong with that. Users who need to use potential new features will have to wait for a new version to adapt, which is very common.

> I disagree with this perspective. If the version field specifically is needed, then I propose that being added.

This is just my personal requirement, and I'm not sure how many others share the same need. However, recently, Headscale has been frequently removing support for backward compatibility with older client versions (which makes sense for maintainability), and I believe we need a convenient way to determine which clients will be broken by updating Headscale (in my case, these are usually clients running on OpenWRT), so we can take preventive measures before updating Headscale.

> I am more conservative to adding it than adding it for the sake of it.

I still don't think being conservative is the best approach. Perhaps it would reduce the maintenance cost of Headscale itself, but it may not be the case for the entire ecosystem. Headplane (one of the popular control panels) is actually considering running a Tailscale client and then using "localapi" to fetch information (tale/headplane#65), but in my view, this would add enough burden to deployment and usage.

Considering that I’ve discovered some new clues, I will request this feature once again and propose providing information equivalent to the following JSON:

[Tailscale API: Get a device​](https://tailscale.com/api#tag/devices/get/device/{deviceId})
